text: Your gold necklace can lose $200 the moment you pay.
Gold didn't fall, so what did?
Next week is Dantaris, India's biggest day for buying gold.
But a $1,000 necklace isn't a $1,000 of gold.
So what are you really paying for?
Making charges, the fee for design and labor,
Then, tax on top. When you sell, most jewelers pay only for the gold inside.
And that's still not the worst part. The making charges? Gone. The tax? Gone.
That's the mirage. You thought you bought gold. Part of your money? Bought art.
So a $1,000 necklace can sell back for around $800, even if gold never moves.
Many savers pick coins or bars instead.
Gold losing value? Best day ever!
Comet, do you buy gold to wear or save?
